item.title: Deploy
item.description:
Deployment guides for getting Workday OfficeConnect into the hands of your finance team, from a handful of users to an enterprise rollout.

Articles in this section

  • Deploy via Registry — Push Workday OfficeConnect tenant configuration to user machines using the Windows registry
  • Intune Win32 Packaging — Package Workday OfficeConnect as a Win32 app for Microsoft Intune, push to all users silently, and verify deployment
  • SCCM / MECM Deployment — Deploy Workday OfficeConnect through Microsoft Configuration Manager (SCCM/MECM) with silent install switches, detection methods, and required user-rights handling

item.title: Get Started
item.description:
OfficeConnect is a Microsoft Office add-in that pulls live data from Workday Adaptive Planning directly into Excel, Word, and PowerPoint. This section covers everything you need to get up and running — from checking system requirements to installing the add-in and verifying your version.

Articles in this section

  • What is OfficeConnect? — An overview of OfficeConnect — what it does, who it’s for, and how it works with Workday Adaptive Planning
  • First 30 Minutes — Install, sign in, build your first report, and refresh it — a complete onboarding path from zero to a live Workday OfficeConnect report in half an hour
  • System Requirements — Hardware and software prerequisites before installing OfficeConnect
  • Install (End User) — Install OfficeConnect on your own machine without requiring IT involvement
  • Install (IT Admin) — Deploy OfficeConnect to multiple users using per-machine installation and group policy or scripts
  • Check Your Version — How to check which version of OfficeConnect you have and update to the latest release

item.title: Configure
item.description:
Tenant configuration, single sign-on, and the network plumbing OfficeConnect needs to reach Workday Adaptive Planning.

Articles in this section

  • Sign In & Create Tenant — Sign in to Workday OfficeConnect for the first time and configure your Workday tenant connection
  • Multiple Instances — How to switch between production, sandbox, and multi-instances in Workday OfficeConnect
  • Workday SSO — Configure Workday OfficeConnect to use Workday Single Sign-On for your organization
  • SSO with Okta — Configure Okta to authenticate Workday OfficeConnect users via Workday SSO — application setup, claim mapping, MFA pairing, and the common failure modes
  • SSO with Microsoft Entra ID — Configure Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure AD) to authenticate Workday OfficeConnect users via Workday SSO — enterprise application setup, claim mapping, and Conditional Access tuning
  • Refresh with Power Automate — Use Power Automate Desktop to schedule Workday OfficeConnect report refreshes automatically — keep distributed Excel reports up to date without manual intervention

item.title: Govern
item.description:
Governance topics for keeping OfficeConnect deployments secure, auditable, and compliant.

Articles in this section

  • Secure Workbooks — How Workday OfficeConnect handles security, timeouts, and data clearing to protect sensitive financial data

item.title: Data Entry & Write-Back
item.description:
Data flows both ways in modern Workday OfficeConnect. Use this section to enter planning data, write back to Adaptive Planning from Excel, design write-back permissions, and recover from common errors.

Articles in this section

  • Enter Budget Data — Use Workday OfficeConnect’s data entry mode to write budget figures directly from Excel into Adaptive Planning — no need to log in to the Adaptive Planning web interface
  • Write-Back Complete Guide — The 2025R1 write-back feature in Workday OfficeConnect — what it does, who can use it, how to set up a write-back workbook, and how to recover when it fails
  • Write-Back Permissions — Design Adaptive Planning permissions so Workday OfficeConnect write-back is safe by default — least-privilege roles, version-state gates, and Level-scoped assignments
  • Write-Back Errors — Diagnose and fix the most common Workday OfficeConnect write-back errors — symptoms, root causes, fixes, and how to prevent each from recurring
  • Write-Back Audit Trail — Where Workday OfficeConnect write-back submissions are logged in Adaptive Planning, what’s captured, and how to build a SOX-grade review process around the audit trail

item.title: Upgrade
item.description:
Workday ships OfficeConnect on a roughly six-month release cadence with mandatory upgrades. These guides help you stay ahead of the prompt.

Articles in this section

Articles for this section are being authored. Check back soon, or browse the main sections from the homepage.

item.title: Admin & Power Users
item.description:
Workday OfficeConnect lives at the intersection of finance and IT. This section is for the people who deploy it, secure it, and keep it running well — whether your title says IT administrator or you’re the FP&A power user everyone turns to when something breaks.

Pick a sub-section:

  • Deploy — install across the organization, package for Intune/SCCM, and choose between per-user and per-machine.
  • Configure — tenant XML, single sign-on with Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, and Ping, plus proxy and firewall allowlists.
  • Govern — licenses, audit logging, secret rotation, tenant migration runbooks.
  • Upgrade — manage the forced-upgrade cadence, prepare users, and roll back when needed.

Articles in this section

Sub-sections

  • Configure — Configure Workday OfficeConnect tenants, single sign-on, multi-instance setups, and network access
  • Deploy — Install Workday OfficeConnect across the organization — silent install switches, Intune Win32 packaging, SCCM, GPO templates, and the per-user vs per-machine decision
  • Govern — Govern Workday OfficeConnect responsibly — secure workbooks, manage licenses, rotate secrets, capture audit trails, and run tenant migrations safely
  • Upgrade — Manage Workday OfficeConnect’s forced-upgrade cadence — version compatibility, user preparation, rollback paths, and multi-region migrations

item.title: Troubleshoot & FAQ
item.description:
Step-by-step fixes for the most common OfficeConnect issues, from installation errors to display problems and data formatting questions.

Articles in this section

  • COM Registration Error — How to resolve COM registration errors when installing or updating OfficeConnect
  • Update Errors — How to fix errors that occur when updating OfficeConnect to a new version
  • Task Pane Issues — How to fix the OfficeConnect Reporting pane when it’s not showing or displaying incorrectly
  • Numbers Not Shifting — Why OfficeConnect elements don’t move when you insert Excel rows, and how to fix it
  • Hide Zeros & Blanks — How to hide rows with all zeros or blank values in your OfficeConnect workbook
  • Remove Elements — How to clear OfficeConnect elements from cells, rows, or columns
  • Rounding Settings — How to change how numbers are rounded in OfficeConnect reports
  • Percentage Values — How to prevent rounding from distorting percentage values in OfficeConnect
  • Fixed Date Columns — How to prevent date columns from rolling forward when using relative time elements
  • Trailing 12-Month Report — How to build a report that always shows the most recent 12 months of data
  • Link External Excel Files — How to link to a plain Excel file from within an OfficeConnect workbook
  • Troubleshooting Tool — How to use the OCSystemChecker tool to generate a diagnostic log for Workday Support
  • Re-Enable Disabled COM Add-in — If Excel disabled Workday OfficeConnect after a crash or stall, the ribbon tab disappears and reinstalling doesn’t help — re-enable it from Excel’s Disabled Items list
  • ‘Contact Technical Support’ on Refresh — The vague “Refresh failed — contact technical support” dialog in Workday OfficeConnect almost always has one of five concrete causes. Diagnose and fix
  • Not Refreshing — OfficeConnect shows stale data or the Refresh button does nothing — causes and step-by-step fixes
  • Authentication and Token Errors — OfficeConnect shows authentication errors, token expired messages, or fails to sign in — causes and step-by-step fixes for SSO and token issues
  • Slow Performance — OfficeConnect refresh takes a long time in large workbooks — diagnose the cause and reduce refresh time
  • Data Discrepancies — OfficeConnect shows different figures than Workday Report Writer or the Workday UI for the same account and period — common causes and how to diagnose them
  • think-cell Conflict — Workday OfficeConnect and think-cell both use Excel COM subclassing and can interfere with each other — refresh failures, broken charts, Excel crashes. Here’s the documented fix
  • OfficeConnect on Mac — Install and use Workday OfficeConnect on a Mac with Excel for Mac — what works, what’s different from Windows, and how to handle common Mac-specific issues
  • Mac VDI Workflow — Mac users can run the full Windows OfficeConnect experience through a VDI like Azure Virtual Desktop, AWS WorkSpaces, or Parallels — here’s the realistic decision guide and setup

item.title: Performance & Optimization
item.description:
A slow OfficeConnect report is usually a design problem, not a product limitation. These guides cover refresh benchmarks, the 32-bit vs 64-bit Excel decision, element-count reduction, and patterns for very large workbooks.

Articles in this section

  • Optimize Performance — Speed up Workday OfficeConnect reports that are slow to refresh — reduce formula count, use efficient time contexts, and configure workbook settings for large Adaptive Planning models
  • Refresh Benchmarks — Rough benchmarks for what a normal Workday OfficeConnect refresh should take by formula count, what moves the numbers, and how to measure your own workbooks
  • 32-bit vs 64-bit Excel — Why 64-bit Excel matters for large Workday OfficeConnect workbooks, how to check which version you’re running, and how to switch without breaking other add-ins
  • Reduce Element Count — Element count is the single biggest performance lever in Workday OfficeConnect — five concrete tactics to cut it without losing the report you need
  • Large Repeating Reports — Patterns and pitfalls for Workday OfficeConnect reports that use repeating rows to generate hundreds of lines from a single element

item.title: Migration & Comparison
item.description:
Whether you’re picking OfficeConnect over the Workday Adaptive Planning web reports, or moving from Hyperion SmartView, OneStream, Vena, or Anaplan — this section helps you choose with eyes open and migrate without rework.

Articles in this section

  • Financials vs Adaptive Planning — Key differences in Workday OfficeConnect behavior depending on whether you’re using the Adaptive Planning or Financials data source
  • OC vs Web Reports — When to use Workday OfficeConnect vs Workday Adaptive Planning’s built-in web reports — a scoring framework with concrete recommendations

item.title: Reference
item.description:
Stable, factual surfaces you’ll come back to. Glossary, formula reference, element-type catalog, version-compatibility matrix, time-context tokens, keyboard shortcuts, ribbon command reference, and network endpoint list.

Articles in this section

  • Glossary — Alphabetical reference for every Workday OfficeConnect term — elements, filters, contexts, write-back, tenants, and more
  • Formula Reference — What’s actually inside a Workday OfficeConnect cell — formula structure, components, and how to read it
  • Element Types — Every element type you can drag from the Workday OfficeConnect Reporting pane, what it represents, and where it lives in each data source
  • Version Compatibility — Which Workday OfficeConnect client versions work with which Workday Adaptive Planning releases — including the forced-upgrade grace periods

item.title: What's New
item.description:
Workday ships OfficeConnect updates on a roughly six-month cadence. This hub tracks every release with a plain-language summary, what changed in the ribbon, and links to deep-dive articles on new features.

Articles in this section

  • 2026R1 Overview — Workday OfficeConnect 2026R1 (released March 14, 2026) introduces View By in the ribbon, personal what-if scenarios for end users, and the latest forced-upgrade prompt at sign-in
  • View By (2026R1) — The 2026R1 View By ribbon command opens the data behind any Workday OfficeConnect cell in a separate worksheet so you can slice and filter without breaking your main report
  • Personal Scenarios (2026R1) — Workday OfficeConnect 2026R1 lets end users create personal what-if scenarios without involving an Adaptive Planning admin — scoped to the individual, branched from a parent version, and invisible to others
